examples.en: The supermarket is discounting processed meat products.
They're processed, so they last longer than fresh ones.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 수산물 가공품도 같이 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop also sells processed seafood products.

examples.ko: 아이에게는 가공품보다 신선한 과일을 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to give my child fresh fruit rather than processed food.
I check the ingredients of processed goods on the packaging.

examples.ko: 농산물 가공품 수출이 늘었다는 소식이 있어요.
examples.en: There is news that exports of processed farm products have grown.

explain: 원래 재료를 손질하거나 만들어 바꾼 물건이에요. 식품에서는 '가공식품'과 함께 많이 쓰고, 반대로 가공하지 않은 것은 '원재료'나 '생것'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to goods made by treating or transforming raw materials. For food it appears together with '가공식품', and unprocessed things are called '원재료' or '생것'.

en: to be alleviated; to be reduced

examples.en: The pain eased after I took the medicine.

examples.ko: 새 제도 덕분에 부담이 많이 경감돼요.
examples.en: Thanks to the new system, the burden is eased a lot.

examples.ko: 세금이 경감되면 생활이 조금 나아질 거예요.
examples.en: If taxes are reduced, life will get a little better.
The doctor said the symptoms have eased.
With less homework, I feel my stress easing.
I'm checking whether the cost will go down.

explain: 덜어지는 쪽에서 말하는 표현이에요. '부담이 경감되다'처럼 말하고, 하는 사람을 말하려면 '경감하다'를 써요. '줄어들다'보다 딱딱하고 좋은 방향의 변화에 어울려요.
explain_en: This is the side of the thing being eased. You say '부담이 경감되다'; to name who does the easing, use 경감하다. It is stiffer than 줄어들다 and fits changes for the better.

en: to be supplied; to be provided

examples.en: Electricity is supplied to every house.
The water was cut off and wasn't supplied.
Fresh vegetables are supplied to the shop every day.

examples.ko: 부품이 제때 공급되면 공장이 계속 돌아가요.
examples.en: If parts are supplied on time, the factory keeps running.
Here there are drinks supplied for free.
The amount supplied fell short, so the price went up.

explain: 전기·물·가스처럼 생활에 필요한 것이 필요한 곳으로 들어오는 상황에 자주 써요. 주는 쪽은 '공급하다'이고, 받는 쪽 입장에서는 '공급받다'예요. 경제에서는 '수요'와 짝이 되어 '수요와 공급'으로 나와요.
explain_en: It is common for utilities like electricity, water and gas reaching where they are needed. The giver's verb is 공급하다 and the receiver's is 공급받다. In economics it pairs with 수요 as '수요와 공급' (supply and demand).

examples.ko: 집을 고치는 데 공사비가 생각보다 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: The construction cost for fixing the house was higher than I expected.
I chose cheap materials to cut construction costs.
I heard the city pays the construction cost of the new road.
The building plan was delayed because of construction costs.
The construction cost is written in detail in the estimate.

examples.ko: 가게를 열기 전에 공사비부터 계산해 봤어요.
examples.en: Before opening the shop, I first calculated the construction cost.

explain: '공사비'는 '공사'와 '비(돈)'가 합쳐진 말이에요. 비슷한 말로 '건축비', '인테리어 비용'이 있어요. 집이나 길을 짓거나 고치는 일에 드는 돈에 두루 써요. '공사비가 들다', '공사비를 아끼다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 공사비 combines 공사 (construction work) and 비 (cost). Similar words are 건축비 and 인테리어 비용. It is used broadly for money spent on building or repairing houses and roads. Common patterns are 공사비가 들다 and 공사비를 아끼다.

en: to tax; to impose a tax

examples.en: The state taxes differently depending on income.
Is value-added tax applied to this product too?
They started taxing rental income too.

examples.ko: 정부가 설탕이 든 음료에 과세하겠다고 발표했어요.
examples.en: The government announced it would tax sugary drinks.

examples.ko: 해외에서 번 돈에도 과세할 수 있어요.
examples.en: They can tax money earned abroad too.
Please explain on what basis they impose the tax.

explain: 말로는 '세금을 매기다'라고 많이 하고, '과세하다'는 뉴스·법·회계에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 반대로 세금을 안 매기는 것은 '면세하다'나 '비과세'라고 해요. '~에 과세하다'처럼 세금이 붙는 대상에 조사 '에'를 써요.
explain_en: In speech people often say '세금을 매기다'; '과세하다' is the stiff word used in news, law and accounting. The opposites are '면세하다' and '비과세' (no tax). The thing being taxed takes the particle '에', as in '~에 과세하다'.

en: advertising expense; advertising cost; advertising fee

examples.en: This month only the advertising cost went up a lot.
A new product came out, so we spent a lot on advertising.
We postponed making the video because the ad budget fell short.
Small shops feel the burden of advertising costs heavily.
How much did advertising cost this month?
The effect is small compared to the advertising cost.

explain: '광고비를 쓰다/들이다/아끼다'처럼 써요. 같은 '-비' 말로 '교통비', '식비'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is used as '광고비를 쓰다/들이다/아끼다'. Other '-비' (cost) words include '교통비' and '식비'.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 모든 메뉴 가격이 균일해요.
examples.en: At this shop, every menu item is the same price.

examples.ko: 반죽을 균일하게 펴야 빵이 고르게 익어요.
examples.en: You have to spread the dough evenly for the bread to bake evenly.

examples.ko: 학생들의 점수가 균일하지 않아서 반을 나눴어요.
examples.en: The students' scores weren't uniform, so we split the class.
I chose wallpaper with an even color.
The items are uniform in size, so they're easy to pack.
I bought a pot that spreads heat evenly.

explain: '고르다'와 비슷하지만 크기, 두께, 가격, 품질처럼 비교할 수 있는 것이 모두 같을 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '고르다'가 더 자연스러워요. 가격을 같게 받는 '균일가'도 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It is similar to '고르다' (even), but is used when things that can be compared, such as size, thickness, price or quality, are all the same. In everyday conversation, '고르다' sounds more natural. Also learn '균일가', meaning one fixed price for everything.

examples.en: House prices are showing a sharp upward trend these days.
Gas prices turned sharply upward, so the burden is big.
There was news that the sharp rise has lost some steam.
The sharp rise in vegetable prices is due to the rainy season.
I was startled by the surge and sold my stocks.
It's in a sharp rise now, so I'm afraid to buy.

explain: '급등세를 보이다/타다/이어가다'처럼 값이 빠르게 오르는 흐름을 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '급락세'이고, 뉴스에서 집값, 주가, 환율 이야기에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It describes a fast upward trend, as in '급등세를 보이다/타다/이어가다'. The opposite is '급락세', and it appears in news about house prices, stocks and exchange rates.

examples.ko: 이 종목은 급상승 뒤에 급락하는 일이 잦아요.
examples.en: This stock often plunges after a sharp rise.

examples.ko: 코인 가격이 급락해서 손해를 본 친구가 많아요.
examples.en: Crypto prices plunged, and many friends lost money.
The stock price suddenly plunged yesterday.
In winter, the temperature often drops sharply.
When popularity plunges, advertising also decreases.

examples.ko: 급락한 가격에 물건을 사려는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people want to buy at the sharply reduced price.

explain: '떨어지다'보다 훨씬 갑작스럽고 크게 내려갈 때 써요. 주가, 가격, 기온, 인기에 쓰고 반대말은 '급등하다'예요.
explain_en: It is much more sudden and large than '떨어지다' (to fall). It is used for stock prices, prices, temperature and popularity, and the opposite is '급등하다'.

examples.en: I learned that paying taxes is a duty of the people.
I file my tax return every May.

examples.ko: 성실하게 납세하는 사람에게 혜택을 주는 나라도 있어요.
examples.en: Some countries give benefits to people who faithfully pay their taxes.

examples.ko: 외국인도 한국에서 돈을 벌면 납세 의무가 생겨요.
examples.en: Foreigners also have a duty to pay taxes if they earn money in Korea.
I needed a tax payment certificate, so I went to the tax office.

examples.ko: 납세자의 날에는 세금을 성실히 낸 사람들에게 상을 줘요.
examples.en: On Taxpayers' Day, awards are given to people who paid their taxes faithfully.

explain: 일상에서는 '세금을 내다'라고 하고, '납세'는 '납세자', '납세 의무', '납세 증명서'처럼 딱딱한 말 속에서 자주 만나요. 비슷한 '납부'는 세금뿐 아니라 요금이나 보험료를 낼 때도 써요.
explain_en: In daily life people say '세금을 내다', while '납세' appears in formal compounds such as '납세자', '납세 의무' and '납세 증명서'. The similar word '납부' is also used for paying bills or insurance premiums, not just taxes.

examples.ko: 우리나라 소득세는 누진세 방식이라 많이 벌수록 세율이 높아져요.
examples.en: Income tax in our country is progressive, so the more you earn, the higher the rate.

examples.ko: 누진세가 너무 높다고 불만인 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people complain that the progressive tax is too high.

examples.ko: 누진세 덕분에 소득 차이가 조금 줄어든다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the income gap narrows a little thanks to progressive taxation.
There was talk on the news about changing the progressive tax.

examples.ko: 저는 누진세에 대해 더 알고 싶어서 책을 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I borrowed a book because I wanted to learn more about progressive taxes.

examples.ko: 월급이 오르면 누진세 때문에 세금도 더 늘어요.
examples.en: When your salary goes up, your taxes rise even more because of the progressive tax.

explain: 전기 요금처럼 쓸수록 단가가 올라가는 방식은 '누진세'가 아니라 '누진제'라고 해요. 발음이 비슷해서 헷갈리지만 '세'는 세금, '제'는 제도예요.
explain_en: A system where the unit price rises the more you use, like electricity rates, is called '누진제', not '누진세'. They sound alike, but '세' means tax and '제' means system.

examples.en: The company announced a wage freeze this year.
Even as prices rose, the bus fare was frozen.
Employees were disappointed by the pay freeze.

examples.ko: 은행 계좌 동결 소식에 사람들이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: People were shocked by the news of the account freeze.

examples.ko: 금리 동결이 시장에 어떤 영향을 줄까요?
examples.en: How will the interest rate freeze affect the market?

examples.ko: 등록금 동결 소식을 듣고 학생들이 안심했어요.
examples.en: Students were relieved to hear the tuition freeze news.

explain: 물가, 월급, 요금처럼 오르내릴 수 있는 것을 그대로 두는 일에 써요. 계좌나 재산을 못 쓰게 묶어 두는 일에도 써요. '동결하다'와 짝으로 외워 두세요.
explain_en: Used when something that could rise or fall, such as prices, pay, or fares, is held where it is. It also covers locking an account or assets so they can't be used. Learn it together with '동결하다'.

examples.en: This shop buys and sells used cars.

examples.ko: 집을 매매할 때는 계약서를 꼼꼼히 봐야 해요.
examples.en: When you buy or sell a house, you need to read the contract carefully.
He made money trading stocks.
A real estate agent helps people buy and sell land.

examples.ko: 허가 없이 동물을 매매하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not trade animals without a permit.

examples.ko: 요즘은 인터넷으로 물건을 매매하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days many people buy and sell things online.

explain: 일상에서는 '사고팔다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '매매하다'는 집, 땅, 차, 주식처럼 큰 거래에서 써요. '부동산 매매', '중고차 매매'처럼 명사 '매매'로 쓰는 일이 더 많아요.
explain_en: In daily life people say 사고팔다 more often; 매매하다 is for bigger deals like houses, land, cars, and stocks. The noun 매매 is even more common, as in '부동산 매매' (real estate sales) and '중고차 매매' (used car trade).

en: item or property for sale; listing

examples.ko: 이 동네는 나온 매물 자체가 별로 없어요.
examples.en: There are hardly any listings at all in this neighborhood.

examples.ko: 중고 사이트에서 마음에 드는 매물을 찾았어요.
examples.en: I found a listing I like on a secondhand site.
Good listings sell as soon as they go up.

examples.ko: 그 차는 매물로 나온 지 일주일 됐어요.
examples.en: That car has been up for sale for a week.

examples.ko: 매물 사진과 실제 모습이 너무 달라서 실망했어요.
examples.en: The listing photos and the real thing were so different that I was disappointed.

examples.ko: 요즘 전세 매물이 부족해서 집 구하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Jeonse listings are scarce these days, so finding a home is hard.

explain: 중고 거래와 집 구하기에서 자주 들려요. '부동산 매물', '매물이 나오다', '매물이 없다'처럼 써요. 사려는 사람은 '매물을 찾다', 파는 사람은 '매물로 내놓다'라고 해요.
explain_en: You hear this a lot in secondhand trading and house hunting, as in '부동산 매물', '매물이 나오다', and '매물이 없다'. A buyer says '매물을 찾다', and a seller says '매물로 내놓다'.

en: to be changed; to be fluctuated

examples.en: Exchange rates change every day.

examples.ko: 시험 일정이 변동되면 바로 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: If the exam schedule changes, I'll let you know right away.
I hope prices don't fluctuate much.

examples.ko: 비행기 표 값은 시기에 따라 변동돼서 미리 사는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Flight ticket prices fluctuate by season, so it's better to buy early.
I saw a notice saying the bus route will change.

examples.ko: 날씨에 따라 가격이 변동될 수 있어요.
examples.en: The price may change depending on the weather.

explain: 값, 수치, 일정이 상황에 따라 오르내리거나 달라질 때 써요. '바뀌다'보다 딱딱해서 환율, 물가, 일정 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요. 안내문에서 '변동 가능'이라고 쓰면 확정이 아니라는 표시예요.
explain_en: Use it when prices, figures, or schedules move up and down or shift depending on circumstances. It is stiffer than 바뀌다 and often pairs with exchange rates, prices, and schedules. '변동 가능' on a notice means it is not final.

en: being non-taxable; being tax-free; being tax-exempt

examples.ko: 이 상품은 이자가 비과세라서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This product is popular because the interest is tax-free.

examples.ko: 비과세 혜택을 받으려면 조건을 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: You need to check the conditions to get the tax-exempt benefit.
I wonder which items are non-taxable in the year-end tax settlement.
The interest on this account is treated as tax-free.
I'm planning to sign up for a tax-free savings account.
Please tell me what the tax-exempt limit is.

explain: 반대말은 '과세'예요. '비과세 혜택', '비과세 상품'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙이거나 '비과세로 처리되다'처럼 써요. '면세'는 '면세점'처럼 물건에 붙는 세금을 면제할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '과세' (taxation). It is used before nouns, as in '비과세 혜택' and '비과세 상품', or in '비과세로 처리되다'. '면세' often appears in words like '면세점' (duty-free shop), where the tax on goods is waived.

examples.en: How much is the meeting room fee per hour?

examples.ko: 이 앱은 사용료를 내야 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to pay a fee to use this app.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 사용료가 싸지만 위치가 불편해요.
examples.en: The fee for this building is cheap, but the location is inconvenient.
You also have to pay the campsite fee in advance.
You only need to pay the usage fee every month.
They maintain the facility with the fees they receive.

explain: '사용료'는 쓴 만큼 내는 돈이고 '이용료'도 거의 같은 상황에 써요. 방이나 땅을 빌릴 때는 '임대료', 물건을 빌릴 때는 '대여료'라고 해요. '사용료를 내다', '사용료를 받다'처럼 같이 써요.
explain_en: 사용료 is money paid for what you use, and 이용료 fits almost the same situations. Renting a room or land is 임대료, and renting an item is 대여료. It pairs with '사용료를 내다' (to pay) and '사용료를 받다' (to charge).

en: to calculate; to compute; to estimate

examples.en: Insurance premiums are calculated differently depending on age.
The way taxes are calculated is complicated.

examples.ko: 피해 금액을 산정한 뒤에 보상을 시작할 거예요.
examples.en: We will start the compensation after we work out the amount of damage.
The monthly rent was set based on the floor area.

examples.ko: 점수를 어떻게 산정할지 먼저 정해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to decide first how to calculate the scores.

examples.ko: 이 요금은 사용량에 맞춰 산정하면 돼요.
examples.en: You can work out this fee according to the amount used.

explain: '계산하다'는 숫자를 더하고 곱하는 일 전반에 쓰고, 산정하다는 요금·세금·보험료·점수처럼 기준을 정해서 값을 매길 때 써요. '비용을 산정하다', '기준으로 산정하다'처럼 말해요. 대화보다 뉴스·계약서·공문에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '계산하다' covers adding and multiplying numbers in general, while '산정하다' is for setting a value by a standard, such as fees, taxes, insurance premiums or scores. Typical uses are '비용을 산정하다' and '기준으로 산정하다'. You see it more in news, contracts and official documents than in conversation.

examples.en: The tax rate went up a little this year.
Tax rates differ by country.

examples.ko: 세율이 낮은 나라로 회사를 옮기는 경우도 있어요.
examples.en: Some companies move to countries with low tax rates.
A high tax rate applies to this item.
The government announced it will lower the tax rate.

examples.ko: 세율을 알아야 정확한 세금을 계산할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You need to know the rate to calculate the exact tax.

explain: '세금'은 내는 돈이고 '세율'은 그 돈을 정하는 비율이에요. '소득세율', '부가가치세율'처럼 앞에 세금 이름을 붙여요. '세율이 오르다/내리다'와 '세율을 올리다/내리다'를 짝으로 외워 두세요.
explain_en: '세금' is the money you pay and '세율' is the rate that decides it. Put the tax name in front, as in '소득세율'. Learn '세율이 오르다/내리다' together with '세율을 올리다/내리다'.

examples.en: Our country imports oil, so it is sensitive to fuel prices.

examples.ko: 한국은 이 과일의 주요 수입국 중 하나예요.
examples.en: Korea is one of the main importing countries of this fruit.
With more importing countries involved, the price went down a little.
It is safer if you increase the variety of importing countries.
I saw on the news which countries import rice.
The importing country raised taxes, so the price of the goods went up.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '수출국'이에요. 뉴스에서는 '주요 수입국', '최대 수입국'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '수출국' (exporting country). In the news it appears as '주요 수입국' (main importing country) or '최대 수입국' (largest importing country).

examples.en: This fruit is imported from the Philippines.
Many new cars were imported last year.
Imported meat is cheaper.

examples.ko: 내일 새 제품이 한국으로 수입될 거예요.
examples.en: The new product will be imported into Korea tomorrow.

examples.ko: 이 커피는 브라질에서 수입돼서 맛이 좋아요.
examples.en: This coffee is imported from Brazil, so it tastes good.

examples.ko: 외국에서 수입된 물건에는 표시가 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: Goods imported from abroad have a label on them.

explain: 반대말은 '수출되다'예요. 물건이 어느 나라에서 들어오는지 말할 때 '~에서 수입되다'로 써요. 마트에서는 '수입산'이라는 말도 자주 보여요.
explain_en: The opposite is 수출되다. You say '~에서 수입되다' to say which country goods come from. At the supermarket you will often see the label 수입산, meaning imported.

examples.ko: 이 공장에서는 부품이 아니라 완제품을 만들어요.
examples.en: This factory makes finished products, not parts.
Finished products are shipped after inspection.

examples.ko: 조립하기 어려우면 완제품을 사는 게 나아요.
examples.en: If assembling is hard, it's better to buy the finished product.

examples.ko: 완제품 가격이 부품 값보다 많이 비싸요.
examples.en: The price of the finished product is much higher than the parts.
We deliver this furniture fully assembled.
Which should we buy, a finished one or an assemble-it-yourself one?

explain: 다 만들어져서 바로 쓸 수 있는 물건이에요. 반대로 '부품', '원자재', 직접 맞추는 '조립식'과 같이 비교해서 많이 써요. 가구나 가전을 살 때 '완제품이에요?'라고 물어볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means an item that is fully made and ready to use. It is often compared with '부품' (parts), '원자재' (raw materials) and '조립식' (assemble-yourself). When buying furniture or appliances you can ask '완제품이에요?'.

examples.en: Insurance rates go up a little from next year.
Each bank's fee rate is slightly different.
I checked the price by looking at the new rate table.
Parcel delivery rates are set according to weight.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 낮은 요율로 서비스를 제공해요.
examples.en: This company provides its service at a low rate.

examples.ko: 새 요율 때문에 이번 달 요금이 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Because of the new rate, this month's bill came out high.

explain: '요금'은 실제로 내는 돈이고, '요율'은 그 돈을 정하는 기준이 되는 비율이나 단가예요. 보험, 수수료, 택배, 전기 같은 이야기에서 뉴스나 안내문으로 많이 만나요. 은행 이자의 비율은 보통 '금리'라고 해요.
explain_en: '요금' is the money you actually pay, while '요율' is the rate or unit price used to set it. You mostly meet it in news and notices about insurance, fees, parcels and utilities. For interest on bank money, people usually say '금리'.

examples.ko: 집을 가진 사람은 매년 재산세를 내야 해요.
examples.en: People who own a house must pay property tax every year.
The property tax bill came as soon as I bought the house.
The property tax notice came in the mail.
Do you know how property tax is calculated?
I inquired at the district office about the property tax.
I almost missed the property tax payment deadline.

explain: 집이나 땅 같은 재산을 가진 사람이 내는 세금이에요. 보통 '재산세를 내다', '재산세가 나오다'처럼 말하고, 소득에 매기는 '소득세'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is the tax paid by people who own property such as a house or land. People say '재산세를 내다' or '재산세가 나오다', and it differs from '소득세' (income tax), which is charged on earnings.

en: to be accumulated; to be credited (points, funds)

examples.ko: 카드로 결제하면 포인트가 자동으로 적립되는 거 알아요?
examples.en: Did you know points are credited automatically when you pay by card?
Pension contributions were put in from this month's salary.
I bought a plane ticket with the accumulated miles.
If you order through the app, one percent will be credited.

examples.ko: 영수증을 보여 주지 않으면 포인트가 적립되지 않아요.
examples.en: Points aren't credited unless you show your receipt.

examples.ko: 통장에 매달 십만 원씩 적립되고 있어요.
examples.en: A hundred thousand won is being saved into the account every month.

explain: 포인트, 마일리지, 연금처럼 쌓이는 것에 써요. 쌓는 사람이 주어이면 '적립하다', 쌓이는 것이 주어이면 '적립되다'예요. 가게에서 '적립해 드릴까요?'라는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is used for things that build up, such as points, miles and pension contributions. When a person does the saving, use 적립하다; when the points themselves are the subject, use 적립되다. In shops you will often hear '적립해 드릴까요?' (Shall I add the points?).

en: to be set; to be allocated (budget, price, wage)

examples.en: A lot of budget was set aside for scholarships this year.

examples.ko: 입장료가 너무 비싸게 책정된 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think the admission fee was set too high.
How is the price of this product set?

examples.ko: 임금은 경력에 따라 책정되는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Wages are often set according to experience.

examples.ko: 새 버스 요금은 아직 책정되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The new bus fare hasn't been set yet.

examples.ko: 행사 예산이 어디에 책정돼 있는지 알아요?
examples.en: Do you know where the event budget has been allocated?

explain: 주어는 보통 가격, 예산, 임금 같은 것이에요. 일상에서는 '정해지다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 사람이 정하는 쪽으로 말할 때는 '책정하다'를 써요.
explain_en: The subject is usually a price, budget or wage. In daily talk '정해지다' is more common, and when you focus on the person who sets it, you use '책정하다'.

examples.ko: 하루에 마시는 물의 총량을 기록해 보세요.
examples.en: Try recording the total amount of water you drink in a day.

examples.ko: 올해 쌀 생산 총량이 지난해보다 늘었어요.
examples.en: The total rice output this year increased from last year.

examples.ko: 음식물 쓰레기의 총량을 줄이는 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We are looking for ways to reduce the total amount of food waste.

examples.ko: 일의 총량은 같은데 사람이 줄어서 힘들어요.
examples.en: The total amount of work is the same but there are fewer people, so it's hard.

examples.ko: 이 통에 담을 수 있는 총량이 얼마예요?
examples.en: What is the total amount this container can hold?

examples.ko: 탄소 배출 총량을 정하자는 이야기가 나와요.
examples.en: There is talk of setting a total limit on carbon emissions.

explain: 전체 양을 숫자로 따질 때 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화보다 뉴스, 보고서, 수업에서 잘 어울려요. '총량을 줄이다/늘리다/정하다'처럼 써요. 일상에서는 '전부 합쳐서'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when counting the whole amount in numbers, so it suits news, reports and lessons better than casual talk. It goes with verbs like '줄이다', '늘리다' and '정하다'. In daily speech people may say '전부 합쳐서' instead.

en: to be depressed; to become stagnant

examples.en: The economy slumped, so the shop's customers decreased.

examples.ko: 분위기가 침체돼서 아무도 말을 안 했어요.
examples.en: The mood sank, so nobody said anything.

examples.ko: 침체된 도시를 살리기 위해 축제를 열어요.
examples.en: They hold a festival to revive the stagnant city.
If the economy stays in a slump for long, jobs decrease.
I sold the shop before the market went into a slump.
It seems that sales will keep stagnating.

explain: 경제·시장·분위기처럼 전체가 활기를 잃고 가라앉았을 때 써요. 사람 기분이 가라앉을 때는 '우울하다'가 더 자연스러워요. '침체하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when something as a whole, such as the economy, a market or a mood, loses energy and sinks. For a person's feelings, 우울하다 sounds more natural. There is also the form 침체하다.

examples.en: Jeju Island's specialty products are tangerines and hallabong.

examples.ko: 여행 가서 그 지역 특산품을 샀어요.
examples.en: On my trip I bought the local specialty.

examples.ko: 이 시장에는 지방 특산품이 많이 있어요.
examples.en: This market has many regional specialties.

examples.ko: 할머니가 고향 특산품을 택배로 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother sent me her hometown's specialty by parcel.
This village is famous for rice as its specialty.

examples.ko: 특산품 가게에서 시식도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can also try samples at the specialty shop.

explain: '제주도 특산품', '지역 특산품'처럼 장소 이름 뒤에 붙여요. 여행에서 사 오는 '기념품'과 달리 그 지역에서 나는 물건이나 음식이에요. '특산물'도 비슷한데 농산물·수산물처럼 자연에서 나는 것에 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It follows a place name: 제주도 특산품, 지역 특산품. Unlike 기념품 (a souvenir), it means something produced in that region. 특산물 is similar but leans toward farm and sea products.

en: goods in kind; the actual item

examples.ko: 월급 대신 현물로 받으면 팔기가 번거로워요.
examples.en: If you're paid in goods instead of a salary, it's a hassle to sell them.

examples.ko: 회사가 명절에 현금 말고 현물을 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: For the holiday, the company handed out goods instead of cash.

examples.ko: 수출할 현물이 창고에 가득 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: The goods to be exported are piled up in the warehouse.

examples.ko: 현물 확인이 어려우면 사진이라도 더 보내 주세요.
examples.en: If it's hard to check the actual item, please send more photos at least.

examples.ko: 현물 사진과 실제 상품이 달라서 실망했어요.
examples.en: The photo of the actual item and the real product were different, so I was disappointed.

examples.ko: 현물은 시세가 바뀌니 값을 미리 정해 두세요.
examples.en: The market price of goods changes, so set the price in advance.

explain: '현금'의 반대 느낌으로, 돈 대신 물건 자체를 말할 때 써요. 온라인 쇼핑에서는 사진과 달리 '실제 물건'이라는 뜻으로 '현물이 더 예뻐요'처럼 말하기도 해요. 경제 뉴스에서는 '현물 시장'처럼 지금 거래되는 실물 이야기에도 나와요.
explain_en: It contrasts with '현금' (cash) and refers to the goods themselves instead of money. In online shopping people also say it to mean the real item as opposed to the photo, as in '현물이 더 예뻐요'. In economic news it appears in phrases like '현물 시장' about physical goods traded now.
